x-moltenterm.group: When he comes to fetch me
x-moltenterm.label: Never come, only the badge
x-moltenterm.description: Master switch: no scene leaves the avatar. The badge keeps counting.

boss:proximity.description: How near Brokk stands. discreet: only the events that matter, no moments and no model call; colleague: he says hello, suggests breaks and lets you know in the evening, and his model may phrase them. Colleague when unset

x-moltenterm.label: Proximity
x-moltenterm.description: How near he stands to you.

x-moltenterm.label: Brainstorms folder
x-moltenterm.description: Where your brainstorms with him are saved, one folder per idea, without asking.

boss:projectsdir.description: The parent folder where a clear brainstorm with Brokk becomes a project, chosen on the project card and then remembered. Each project still asks for its click. Gold, dev and local builds only

x-moltenterm.label: Projects folder
x-moltenterm.description: Where a clear brainstorm becomes a project folder, once you click to make it.

boss:autoapprove.description: Approve without asking the requests of Brokk's agent that stay in his own folder (reading and editing his files, simple read-only commands, git status, diff, log, show, tests), each one shown as a line in his talk window; everything else still asks. Counts only once confirmed in MoltenTerm's settings. Off when unset

x-moltenterm.label: Approve his agent's requests without asking
x-moltenterm.description: Only what stays in his own folder goes without asking, each a line in his window; the rest still asks.

moltenterm:settingsreveal.description: A settings block opened in the library is revealed by molten flows that cool and break open, under 700 ms; false, or reduced motion, fades it in instead

x-moltenterm.label: Molten reveal of settings
x-moltenterm.description: A settings block opened in the library pours, cools and breaks open. Off, or with reduced motion, it fades in.

moltenterm:theme.description: The interface's theme. dark (the default when unset), light, or system to follow the computer's light or dark setting. Terminals keep their own terminal theme, dark by default, in every interface theme

x-moltenterm.label: Theme
x-moltenterm.description: The interface's colours. Terminals stay dark unless you pick a light terminal theme.

moltenterm:view360.description: When a tab with several columns shows in 360 view (its first column fixed, the other panels on a carpet that scrolls sideways). auto: beyond the screen's column threshold or when a panel would fall under its readable width, back when everything fits again. grid (Keep the grid): the panels stay side by side, only columns that cannot fit even at their readable widths still switch. always: every tab with several columns. Unset behaves as auto and asks once which to keep: a view that never was in 360 view is offered the choice, with a number of visible panels, when it first goes beyond the threshold (#2180), and any other view at its first automatic switch; a stored never reads as auto. A tab's own 360 button also turns it on on demand

x-moltenterm.label: 360 view
x-moltenterm.description: When a tab fixes its first column and lays the others on a sideways carpet. Its 360 button turns it on too.

moltenterm:view360places.description: With the 360 view setting on auto: how many panels stay visible on the right of the first column (360 × N) when a view goes beyond the screen's column threshold (1, 2 or 3; a string, as the settings choices are). Unset: the plain 360 view. The first-time offer's check, Do the same in every view, stores it

x-moltenterm.label: Visible panels when it switches by itself
x-moltenterm.description: With Automatic: how many panels stay visible beside the first column. Empty: the plain 360 view.

moltenterm:terminalscreenreader.description: Terminal screen reader support: auto follows system detection on macOS and Windows; on or off overrides detection. Applies immediately to existing terminals without restarting sessions. On is available when automatic detection is unavailable

x-moltenterm.label: Screen reader support
x-moltenterm.description: Automatic follows system detection. On and Off override it, without restarting terminals.

moltenterm:codingagent.description: The coding agent MoltenTerm starts on its own (reviews: investigate, rebase, restart work, batch merge, the assisted review; the release notes; the companion's Start the agent here) when a project chose none in a panel's options: claude (Claude Code) or codex (Codex). Unset: the first installed of Claude Code, then Codex. A chosen agent that is not installed is reported, never replaced

x-moltenterm.label: Default coding agent
x-moltenterm.description: The agent MoltenTerm starts for reviews, release notes and the companion when a project chose none.

moltenterm:reviewssort.description: How the Integration panel sorts its pull requests: state (by state, the default when unset) or merge (the suggested merge order, which reruns the fewest CI runs). Set by the panel's switch

moltenterm:reviewsfolds.description: The Integration panel's sections the developer opened (true) or folded (false), by section: yours, ready, agents, blocked, waiting, notes, leftovers, upcoming, merged. A section not listed follows its default. Set by the sections' headers

moltenterm:settingstab.description: The tab the Settings screen opens on: the one the developer chose last (overview when unset). Set by the screen's tabs

moltenterm:materialsseen.description: When the developer last saw each project's materials, by project, in milliseconds since 1970: newer materials are counted as new in the library. Set by opening the materials section
